name: Infernogallus
sum: Small caenagnathid from the Maastrichtian Hell Creek Formation of the United States, with the first nearly complete articulated skull known for its family.
wsnote: Body mass estimated at about 12 kg (Wikipedia revision 1385853061, from the description); no length given in the sources consulted.
holotype: ROM VP 65050, a partial articulated skeleton in a sandstone concretion (nearly complete skull and mandible, cervical and dorsal series, right pectoral girdle and forelimb, part of the pelvis and right hindlimb), Garfield County, Montana.
material: Four further specimens from Montana, South Dakota and North Dakota (ROM VP 64193, 64194, 88690; NDGS 4351), mostly jaw and palate elements, assigned as paratypes.
biology: The skull shows a reorganisation of the jaw muscles that the describers interpret as an adaptation for eating fruit, similar to some parrots but unique among non-avian theropods.
author: Funston et al. 2026

sources.text: Funston GF, Dudgeon TW, Simon DJ, Dufault DM, Boyd C, Fowler D, Currie PJ, Evans DC 2026. Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda). Nature communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78343-w

dates_note: No PBDB record. Hell Creek Formation is Maastrichtian (Wikipedia revision 1385853061); the ICS bounds of the stage are used.
